before: A w:sym had no model offset width. Paragraph text skipped it, the caret could not step over it, and only a deletion spanning it removed it.
after: A w:sym is one model character that reads as "(". It selects and deletes like a hyphen element, and search never matches it.
reason: Shared state is unchanged: a symbol stays a generic tree node with the same identity and journal operations, and text effects address textValue positions, which do not count it. Model offsets do count each symbol now. In a room that mixes released and current participants, a remote caret placed after a symbol in the same paragraph shows one position off; presence is ephemeral and the saved room is unaffected. Experimental per-paragraph text collaboration carries a symbol as "(" and cannot recreate it from text: an update that changes two separate regions of one paragraph replaces the text between them and turns a symbol there into a parenthesis. Before this change the same update deleted the symbol. That lane has its own contract and is not covered by the document format.
